Five habits that made my small team faster

None of these are new, and none of them needed a tool. They are simply the five things that, looking back over two years, made the most difference for the least effort.

1. Write the announcement first

Before anyone opens an editor we write the two paragraphs we would send to customers. If we cannot, the work is not ready to start.

2. One owner per decision

Everyone may argue, but one named person decides, and writes the decision down where the rest of us can find it next year.

3. Demo on Thursdays

A demo the day before the week ends leaves a day to fix what the demo revealed. Friday demos only reveal it to the weekend.

4. Delete the dashboard nobody opens

We counted visits for a month and removed every chart with fewer than three. Nobody noticed, and the two that remained finally got read.

5. Keep a list of what you stopped doing

It is the only record that the team ever learned anything, and it is the first page we show to somebody new.
